findings.title: A session's collateral tail takes the first 5 ₳ that fits the collateral rule, whoever's it is, so a stranger's plain 5 ₳ listed first is boxed and the session's own collateral comes back unmixed
findings.scenario: Raised by the WebAssembly fixer (G3) from T1f's notes, and by the completeness critic, who called X2's judgment on it ('W1b's direct_tail pointer holds as written; the privacy cost is marginal next to a direct return's rest') a judgment, not a trace. lovejoin.rs's direct_tail (find it by name) puts a private session's 5 ₳ collateral into a Lovejoin box once the chain's mixes no longer need it (the collateral tail, mix_giveme). It takes the first UTxO at the session's account that fits the collateral rule (5 ₳ of ADA alone, no script, no datum), whoever's it is. A stranger who pays the session's one-time account a plain 5 ₳ (a site learns the address once connected; anyone sees it on chain once funded) and is listed first gets that UTxO boxed in place of the session's own collateral, so the session's collateral, which ties to the funding, comes back unmixed (directly, tied to the session), on the default path through Lovejoin. Check: is that what happens; what it ties that privacy.md says is hidden; whether the session's own collateral is then mixed later or never; whether the order Koios lists rows in lets the stranger's row come first.
findings.evidence: G3's note (review-51/fixes and its report): 'T1f's untested note on direct_tail in lovejoin.rs: it takes the first UTxO that fits the collateral rule, whoever's it is, so a stranger's plain 5 ₳ listed first would be boxed and the session's own collateral would come back unmixed. A possible privacy downgrade for 5 ₳, worth a verifier's look.' The critic's weak-claims list on X2's direct_tail line.
findings.fix: Take the session's own collateral (the funding's 5 ₳ output, which the session records) for the tail, never another UTxO that merely fits the rule; a stranger's 5 ₳ goes back as any stranger's money does.
findings.known_check: Not in INDEX.md; X2's coverage judged it without a trace.

notes: Written by the lead from G3's note and the critic's weak-claims list, so that it is verified as any medium is.
